name: Potato slices / juice

lead: Raw potato slices or grated-potato juice are a folk remedy for dark circles and puffiness. Proponents describe them as a natural lightener and cooling compress.
No published study was found testing potato for this purpose.

paras: Believers say compounds in raw potato lighten pigment, and slices applied cold may soothe the area. These mechanisms have not been tested on under-eye skin.

No safety data were found for this use. Raw potatoes contain glycoalkaloids such as solanine and chaconine, which rise in green or damaged tubers; whether skin application matters has not been studied. Contact irritation is possible with any raw plant material.

lead: Potato slices or juice refers to the folk practice of placing thin slices of raw potato, or applying grated or juiced potato, to the skin under the eyes with the aim of lightening dark circles or reducing puffiness. It circulates in home-remedy and beauty communities.

Proponents describe potato as a natural skin lightener and a cooling compress. No clinical study of potato applied to the periorbital area was found, and reference articles on dark circles do not list it among evaluated treatments.[1]
Raw potatoes contain toxic glycoalkaloids, mainly solanine and chaconine, whose levels are higher in tubers exposed to light, damaged or aged.[2]

paras: Practitioners say the slices or juice lighten pigment and reduce swelling. The cooling effect of a refrigerated slice is often cited alongside; see the entry on cold compresses.
Potatoes contain glycoalkaloids, concentrated in skin and increased by light exposure, damage and age.[2] No study was found of their effect when applied to eyelid skin.
